newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian liberals worried by union with Belarus.
newsitem.headline: Russian liberals worried by union with Belarus.

text.p: Prominent Russian liberal leaders expressed concern on Sunday that President Boris Yeltsin was moving towards integration with Belarus too fast and not consulting the Russian people properly.

Yeltsin is due to sign an agreement with Belarus' hardline President Alexander Lukashenko on Wednesday forging closer ties between the two former Soviet republics, but details of the document have not been widely published.

"It would be an unprecedented event to try to ratify such an agreement in parliament without any kind of consideration of this document," Grigory Yavlinksy, leader of the liberal Yaboko bloc, told NTV commercial television.
He made clear Yabloko would vote against the document in the opposition-dominated lower house of parliament, where his bloc has just under 10 percent of the seats.
Yegor Gaidar, a leading liberal and a former acting prime minister, said he supported closer integration with Belarus but not the way it was being carried out.
"The least that should have been done was to publish it (the document), consider it calmly and not rush into signing it," he told Russia Television in an interview.

Russian liberals have also cast doubts on Lukashenko's commitment to human rights and media freedoms, and have expressed concern that the integration process might one day allow him to come to power in Moscow.
Wednesday's document is to be signed on the first anniversary of an agreement by Lukashenko and Yeltsin on April 2 last year to form a "community" between their two Slav states.

Few concrete steps have been taken towards this community but Yeltsin has raised the possibility of Russia and its small western neigbour having one government with a single budget and currency, taxation laws and united fuel and energy systems.
Kremlin aide Sergei Shakhrai defended the new agreement, dismissing fears that Russians would wake up in a new state the day after the agreement was signed.
"This is an inter-state union to which Russia and Belarus delegate part of their powers, which is fully in line with the constitutions of Russia and Belarus," he told Russia Television.
Shakhrai also dismissed fears that Russian interests could ever be disregarded by a nine-member council which will be handed responsibilities for overseeing the Russia-Belarus union.
